column3: The Hebrew joins crossing and the inheritance remaining with them by “and”; BSB expresses the inheritance as a purpose, “that we may have.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite”; BSB uses plural “the Amorites.”
The Hebrew repeats the naming root in “called by names the names of the cities” and says they “built” them; BSB says they “renamed” cities they “rebuilt.”
The Hebrew changes from plural going and capturing to singular driving out, and uses singular collective “the Amorite”; BSB keeps the actions and Amorites plural.
The Hebrew names Machir without an explicit “clan” and uses singular “he dwelt”; BSB supplies “the clan of” Machir and uses plural “they settled.”
The Hebrew calls Jair “a son of Manasseh”; BSB says “a descendant of Manasseh.”
The Hebrew calls the dependent settlements Kenath’s “daughters”; BSB says “its villages.”
